assumptions: Because the NL did not specify a distinct completion event for AutocontrolInit, the candidate uses an immediate bare transition from AutocontrolInit to AutocontrolNormal to make normal autocontrol reachable.
CA_mode is encoded as an int with 0 representing Manual and 1 representing Autocontrol, because the parseable subset supports int/float variables only.
The inverse relationship between blood pressure and flow rate is modeled as flow_rate = target_bp - blood_pressure; the NL did not provide a precise clinical control formula or saturation bounds.
Pump fault occurrence is modeled as an input flag pump_fault rather than a discrete occlusion event, because the NL names pump fault as a condition/complication.
Log-file recording is abstracted as incrementing log_count during normal autocontrol because the DSL has no file I/O primitive.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: At run time, CARA coordinates the Caregiver Interface, Blood Pressure Monitor, Algorithm, and Pump Monitors around an infusion pump.
In the Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy, CARA has manual and autocontrol-related mode-control states plus an Ask_StartAC submode.
The pump has manual and autocontrol modes. In manual mode, pump speed is set with the built-in switch.
CARA has ... an Ask_StartAC submode; within Ask_StartAC, the setpoint can be changed and pressing StartAC enters AutocontrolInit.
During normal autocontrol, CARA controls flow rate only while there are no pump-operation complications.
If a pump fault such as fluid-tubing occlusion occurs, the pump activates alarm signals.
Patient blood pressure is used to compute the infusion rate.
